trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: Earn the platinum trophy by completing all 54 other trophies in the game. The platinum is awarded automatically upon earning the final missing trophy. No specific method — just play through the game and complete everything else first. This includes the platinum roadmap trophy itself, which pops at the very end of your complete GTA VI experience. Track your progress via the in-game statistics menu.
trophies.tip: Use a New Game+ run or a detailed checklist to ensure you don't miss any missable trophies on your first playthrough.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Complete the opening mission "Gone Fishing" which begins GTA VI's story. This tutorial mission introduces the fishing mechanic and awards the Just Like Paradise bronze trophy upon finishing the sequence on Ocean Beach. The mission is linear and unavoidable during the game's opening hours, requiring only that you follow on-screen prompts to catch a fish and progress the story.
trophies.tip: Follow the on-screen prompts during the fishing sequence — you'll need to catch a fish to progress the mission.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Complete all missions and activities in Chapter 1 of GTA VI. Chapter 1 begins with "Gone Fishing" (trophy 2) and concludes after the mission "Down to Earth," which marks the end of the first story chapter. All chapter 1 missions are story-driven and must be completed in sequence — there are no missable objectives within Chapter 1 itself, as every mission progression is automatic and forced by the narrative.
trophies.tip: Chapter 1 is linear story content — just follow the main mission markers to complete it. No missable content within the chapter itself.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Complete all missions and activities in Chapter 2 of GTA VI. Chapter 2 begins with "What's in the Bag?" and features Lucia's storyline involving drug trafficking operations across Leonida. The chapter's missions are story-progressive and must be completed in order; each mission unlocks the next, with no missable content that can be permanently failed or skipped during normal chapter progression.
trophies.tip: Follow the main mission markers for Chapter 2. The missions are progressively unlocked as you complete previous ones.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete all missions and activities in Chapter 3 of GTA VI. Chapter 3 begins with "Welcome to Vice City" and introduces the main heist missions that define the mid-game experience. Chapter 3 missions are fully story-progressive — each completed mission automatically triggers the next, and no content within the chapter can be missed or failed permanently, as all objectives are forced by the narrative sequence.
trophies.tip: Follow the main mission markers for Chapter 3. Some missions may have multiple approaches — choose what suits your playstyle.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Complete all missions and activities in Chapter 4 of GTA VI. Chapter 4 begins with "Ocean Beach" and "Another Life" and concludes with the final mission "Starting From Zero." This is the longest chapter, containing many heist missions and the game's climactic story sequences. All chapter 4 missions are story-progressive and must be completed in sequence; there are no missable objectives that can be permanently skipped within the chapter itself.
trophies.tip: Chapter 4 is the longest chapter with many heist missions. Pay attention to mission markers and follow the story progression.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission "Starting From Zero" which concludes the main story of GTA VI. This is the game's ending mission, serving as the narrative climax. The mission is unavoidable for players who complete the main story, and it awards the gold trophy naturally. There is no way to miss this trophy if you finish the game's story, as it plays at the end of the narrative sequence regardless of prior choices.
trophies.tip: This is a story mission that you'll naturally play through as part of completing the game. Focus on story progression.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the Breakfast Run mission in GTA VI. This early-game mission tasks the player with delivering breakfast items for a character and is part of the main narrative sequence. The mission is story-driven and unlocks as part of the early chapters — it is guaranteed upon progressing through the game and cannot be permanently missed or failed. Breakfast Run introduces basic game mechanics and is the first of many story missions that progressively unlock as you advance through the early chapters of GTA VI.
trophies.tip: Follow the main mission markers for the early game chapter — Breakfast Run is unavoidable during the opening hours.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist mission in GTA VI. This major story mission involves executing a heist for the cartel and is a narrative-driven objective that progresses the game's plot. The heist mission is story-progressive and must be completed in sequence — it is guaranteed upon reaching the appropriate point in the main storyline, with no way to permanently miss or fail the objective during normal play.
trophies.tip: The Cartel Heist mission is part of the main story sequence — progress naturally through the chapters to earn it.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the Child's Play mission in GTA VI. This story mission is a narrative-driven objective that progresses the game's plot and is part of the main chapter sequence. Child's Play unfolds automatically as part of story progression, and the trophy is awarded naturally upon completion — there is no way to miss or permanently fail this mission. Child's Play is typically one of the early chapter missions that sets up subsequent narrative events, and it awards the trophy naturally when you follow the main mission markers through the game's chapter progression.
trophies.tip: Just follow the main mission markers — Child's Play unfolds automatically as part of story progression.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the Headliners mission in GTA VI. This narrative-driven mission is a story-progressive objective that advances the game's plot. Headliners is part of the main chapter sequence and must be completed in order — the trophy is awarded naturally upon finishing the mission, with no way to permanently miss or fail it during normal play. Headliners typically becomes available in the mid-game chapter sequence and is a forced narrative objective that you cannot skip or miss if you are progressing through the main story.
trophies.tip: Complete it naturally as part of chapter progression — Headliners is a story-progressive mission.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the VCIA Takedown mission in GTA VI. This story mission is a narrative-driven objective that progresses the game's plot and is part of the main chapter sequence. VCIA Takedown unfolds automatically as part of story progression, and the trophy is awarded naturally upon completion — there is no way to miss or permanently fail this mission. VCIA Takedown is typically a mid-chapter mission that is part of the main storyline and will award the trophy naturally as you progress through the game's narrative sequence without any risk of permanent failure.
trophies.tip: It will award naturally when you reach the right point in the story — VCIA Takedown is part of the main chapter sequence.

Operation Savage Glory unfolds automatically as part of story progression, and the trophy is awarded naturally upon completion — there is no way to miss or permanently fail this mission.
trophies.tip: Operation Savage Glory unfolds automatically as part of the main story — no extra steps needed.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Attain 100% completion in GTA VI by discovering and completing all game content. This includes all story missions, side activities, collectibles, challenges, and secrets across Leonida Island. The 100% completion roadmap spans all five platinum phases, requiring careful attention to missable trophies (especially Positive Mental Attitude and Strangers & Freaks). Track progress via the in-game completion percentage and consult guides for any remaining items or challenges. New Game+ can help recover any missed content from a first playthrough.
trophies.tip: Track your in-game completion percentage and consult guides for any remaining items or challenges after story completion.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts across Leonida's various stunt locations. Stunts include jumps, tricks, and other aerial or ground maneuvers performed while driving or riding. The game tracks stunt completions in the statistics menu. This is a significant grind that typically requires dedicated playtime — plan to visit stunt locations across all chapters, and consider replaying in New Game+ if you fall short of 250 during a first run.
trophies.tip: Plan to visit stunt locations across all chapters, and consider replaying in New Game+ if you fall short of 250.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once in GTA VI. Activities include races, stunt challenges, drone races, fishing, arcade games, and more. The game features a diverse activity roster, and this trophy pops once you've engaged with every activity type at least once. Most activities become available through natural story progression, but some unlock later in the game, so keep an eye on mission progression and the in-game activity menu.
trophies.tip: Most activities become available through natural story progression — keep an eye on the in-game activity menu.

trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges in GTA VI. Visit the shooting range early and practice each challenge type. Gold medals can be replayed if missed, but they require consistent aim and reaction time. Consider replaying in New Game+ if you struggle on your first attempt.
trophies.tip: Visit the shooting range early and practice each challenge type; gold medals can be replayed if missed.

trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge in GTA VI. The fishing mini-game becomes available through story progression, and Cal is one of the characters who offers fishing challenges. Challenges become available through natural story progression and exploration. If you miss any, they can typically be replayed or farmed in the same areas after story completion.

The partner must survive the escape. This is naturally achieved during story progression, particularly in the later chapters when partner mechanics unlock. If missed, the partner wanted level mechanic can be triggered again in New Game+.
trophies.tip: The partner wanted level mechanic can be triggered again in New Game+ if missed during normal play.

Combat Focus is available through story progression, and the best opportunities arise during enemy ambushes or gang wars. If you miss this during normal play, it can be farmed in areas with frequent enemy encounters, such as combat zones or strongholds.

The contact list becomes available through story progression, so unlock more contacts as you advance the storyline to access more laundering opportunities.
trophies.tip: Multiple smaller laundering transactions add up to $250,000 — the contact list unlocks through story progression.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops in GTA VI. This accumulates across all purchases — clothing, weapons, vehicles, property, and other items from various shops across Leonida. Each shop purchase adds to the total, and the $100,000 threshold comes from many small purchases accumulating over normal play. Track spending via the in-game bank statement. The $100,000 accumulates quickly from normal gameplay — no need to deliberately spend, just play normally.
trophies.tip: Track spending via the in-game bank statement — $100,000 accumulates quickly from normal gameplay.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties in GTA VI. Garage properties are real estate locations across Leonida that can be purchased. All 8 must be bought for this trophy. Garage properties vary in price and become available through story progression. Some early garages become available mid-game, while others are only accessible late in the game. Check the property menu regularly and purchase garages as they become available — don't miss the early ones, as some late-game garages may be missable without a New Game+ replay.
trophies.tip: Purchase garages as they become available through story progression — don't miss the early ones.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app in GTA VI. The Scooter Bros app becomes available through story progression. Register vehicles by finding them and adding them to the app. Each registered vehicle counts toward the 10 total, and any vehicle type counts. The 10 vehicles can be collected over time through free-roam. The Scooter Bros app and vehicle registration are available after the relevant story milestone, so progress naturally through the game.
trophies.tip: Use the Scooter Bros app regularly as you explore Leonida — any vehicle type counts toward the 10 total.
